Common Cause v. Union of India

s:

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because compensation was imposed instead of ordering closure in every case.

a mandatory feature of the EIA Notification, 2006

s:
With reference to the Vanashakti litigation, consider the following statements:
1. The May 2025 ruling struck down the 2017 Notification and the 2021 Office Memorandum.
2. In November 2025, the ruling was recalled by a 2:1 majority.
3. The recall relied, among other decisions, on D. Swamy (2021) and Pahwa Plastics (2022).
4. Approximately ₹20,000 crore worth of projects was reported to be at stake.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All four statements are correct. The May 2025 ruling struck down the specified instruments, was recalled in November 2025 by a 2:1 majority, relied on the cited earlier cases, and affected projects valued at approximately ₹20,000 crore.
tq: Track multiple stages of a case without confusing the original ruling with its recall.

s: Which one of the following correctly states the effect of the final Vanashakti verdict of 29 July 2026?
o: It retrospectively validated all clearances obtained under the 2021 Office Memorandum.
It prospectively nullified the 2021 Office Memorandum, while earlier clearances under the 2017 Notification and 2021 Office Memorandum survived.
It made the 2017 Notification available to all fresh violators seeking regularisation.
It permanently prohibited the Centre from issuing any time-limited notification under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
x: The final verdict prospectively nullified the 2021 Office Memorandum, but earlier environmental clearances under the 2017 Notification and 2021 Office Memorandum survived. It did not open those instruments to fresh violators or permanently bar time-limited notifications under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
tq: Distinguish prospective effect, retrospective validation and future eligibility.
sec: Post-facto clearance and exemption cases - Vanashakti, Noble M. Paikada, Common Cause, Alembic  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements concerning the legal principles stated in the final Vanashakti verdict:
1. Administrative orders cannot override the EIA Notification, 2006.
2. The Central Government may issue time-limited notifications under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
3. Ex post facto environmental clearance must satisfy Articles 14 and 21.
4. The Supreme Court retains power under Article 142.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All four statements correctly state principles associated with the final Vanashakti verdict. Administrative orders cannot override the EIA Notification, 2006, while the stated constitutional and Article 142 principles continue to apply.
tq: Test constitutional provisions and institutional powers through a complete statement combination.
sec: Post-facto clearance and exemption cases - Vanashakti, Noble M. Paikada, Common Cause, Alembic  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following statements regarding fresh violators after the final Vanashakti verdict is NOT correct?
o: Fresh violators can automatically obtain regularisation by paying penalties under the 2021 Office Memorandum.
Fresh violators cannot seek regularisation under the 2017 Notification.
The Centre may issue time-limited notifications under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
Fresh violators cannot seek regularisation under the 2021 Standard Operating Procedure.
x: Fresh violators cannot seek regularisation under the 2017 Notification or the 2021 SOP. Automatic regularisation merely through payment of penalties under the 2021 Office Memorandum is not available to them.
tq: Identify the option that reverses the ruling’s distinction between earlier clearances and fresh violations.

o: Environmental Impact Assessment — Combined effect of several projects in one basin
Strategic Environmental Assessment — Policies, plans and programmes upstream of projects
Life-Cycle Assessment — Compliance check of an operating unit after the fact
Environmental audit — Impacts of a product from raw material extraction to disposal

s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Tool)
a. Environmental Impact Assessment
b. Life-Cycle Assessment
c. Cumulative Impact Assessment
d. Environmental audit

List-II (Scope)
i. Compliance check of an operating unit after the fact
ii. A product or process across its whole life cycle
iii. A project evaluated before it starts
iv. Combined effect of several projects in one area or basin

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: EIA concerns a project before it starts; LCA covers a product or process through its life cycle; cumulative impact assessment examines combined effects; and an environmental audit checks an operating unit after the fact.

s: A government is assessing the environmental implications of a new transport policy before individual road projects are selected. Which tool is most appropriate?
x: Strategic Environmental Assessment examines policies, plans and programmes upstream of individual projects. A project-level EIA is conducted for a specific project, whereas an environmental audit is generally an after-the-fact compliance check.
tq: Identify the level of decision-making before choosing between project and strategic assessment.

s: Which of the following is the most appropriate tool for examining the combined environmental effects of several dams located within the same river basin?
o: Strategic Environmental Assessment of a single product
x: Cumulative Impact Assessment examines the combined effect of several projects in a defined area or basin. It is particularly suited to assessing effects that may not be apparent from separate project-level studies.
tq: Use the geographical and multi-project clues to select cumulative assessment.
sec: EIA vs related tools - SEA, LCA, Cumulative Impact Assessment, environmental audit  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes EIA from LCA?
o: EIA evaluates a product from raw material to disposal, whereas LCA evaluates only a project before construction.
EIA evaluates a project before it starts, whereas LCA evaluates a product or process across its entire life cycle.
EIA is concerned with policies and programmes, whereas LCA is concerned only with public hearings.
Both EIA and LCA are compliance checks conducted only after operations begin.
x: EIA focuses on the impacts of a specific project before it starts. LCA considers the impacts of a product or process across its whole life cycle, from raw materials through disposal.
tq: Separate the object and time frame of assessment rather than treating the tools as interchangeable.
sec: EIA vs related tools - SEA, LCA, Cumulative Impact Assessment, environmental audit  [APPSC]

s: Cleaner production is best described as a strategy that:
o: Treats pollution only after it has been generated at the end of a pipe
Cuts waste and pollution at the source through process change or input substitution
Replaces environmental assessment with an operating-unit audit
Focuses exclusively on disposal of hazardous waste
x: Cleaner production is preventive: it reduces waste and pollution at source through measures such as process change and input substitution, rather than relying mainly on end-of-pipe treatment.

Increase the use of hazardous substances for higher efficiency
Transfer all pollution from production to disposal
Avoid consideration of raw materials and solvents

4. Both cleaner production and green chemistry seek to reduce impacts at the design stage.

s: How do cleaner production and green chemistry relate to EIA and LCA?
o: They increase residual impacts so that EIA and LCA can identify more mitigation measures.
They eliminate the need to assess alternatives in location and process technology.
They make EIA applicable only after a project has started.
They shrink impacts at the design stage, enabling EIA and LCA to find fewer residual impacts requiring mitigation.
x: Cleaner production and green chemistry reduce impacts during design, so EIA and LCA identify fewer residual impacts that require mitigation. EIA nevertheless continues to require assessment of alternatives in location and process technology.
tq: Test the causal link between preventive design and the residual-impact stage of assessment.
